editorial.headline: Cassava Farming, Open Nationally and Workable in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 01135 covers cassava and related tuber cultivation from land preparation through post-harvest, open across all business scales and not blocked for Bali PMA registration.
editorial.body:
**KBLI 01135 is an agricultural production code for cassava farming and the wider cultivation of palawija tubers when the work is run as one integrated activity.** Its scope starts at the soil: land preparation, planting, maintenance, harvesting, and post-harvest handling are all included when they belong to the same cultivation chain. In plain English, this is not a trading code and not a detached processing category. It is for the farming activity itself, with post-harvest work only inside the same agricultural sequence.

The record also gives this code a broader tuber-seed and tuber-crop character. It covers seed and nursery activity for mixed palawija tubers, including cassava, sweet potato, taro, ganyong and irut, gembili, iles-iles, porang, and other similar tuber crops, again from land preparation through planting, care, harvesting, and post-harvest where those steps form a single activity. That matters because a founder registering under this code should be describing a cultivation operation, not merely a distribution desk or a standalone downstream product business.

On scale, the code is unusually straightforward: it is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar businesses. Nationally, the foreign-investment picture is also clear. The slim record marks PMA status as TERBUKA and gives the foreign ownership ceiling as 100, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. For a foreign-owned setup, that means the record itself does not impose a foreign-share cap below full ownership. The honest reading is therefore not a partial-opening story; nationally, this activity is open to PMA up to 100% foreign ownership.

The Bali picture is often where agricultural codes become less intuitive, but this record is explicit. Bali’s moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the province, permanently, according to the cited gubernatorial letter. KBLI 01135 is not marked as blocked in Bali. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the reason given is that OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by the moratorium. The clean conclusion is that a foreign investor is not barred from registering this activity in Bali on the moratorium ground stated in the record. The national door is open, the foreign ceiling is 100%, and the Bali note does not turn that opening into a local block.
